correctness.rationale: At n=1 the empty sum is 0, different from S(2)=2; two primes have distinct sums. In the prime/semiprime orientations, equality and adjacency give (a−1)(b−1)=2 or 0 respectively. Only the first is possible, with factors 2 and 3, giving (5,6), which checks. For semiprime/semiprime, the frozen integer factorization t(b−a−t)=1 follows from a+b=c+d and cd−ab=1. Sorting a≤b excludes the negative factorization; the positive one gives b=a+2 and c=d=a+1, impossible for three consecutive primes. An independent parity check gives the same exclusion: the sum of the two prime factors of an odd semiprime is even, so the even semiprime would have to be 4 (any other has factors 2 and an odd prime), whose neighbours are both prime. Finally S(8)=S(9)=6 and the two multiplicities are 3 and 2. Independent prime-power accumulation on n≤2,000,000 confirms 215 total equal-sum pairs, only (5,6) in the low layer, and the indicated sharp witness. Replay: python /workspace/checks/adjacent_audit.py. This sweep is only corroborative.
residual_risks: The frozen proof omits explicit mention of n=1 in its case split; the empty-sum check handles it. No conclusion about higher layers follows except the exhibited witness.
